server.name: community-solhint
server.version: solhint-mcp (npm latest at image build time)
server.note: Drawn in frame order from block 4 of Frame 3. Seven tools, none of them annotated. It bundles a Solidity linter and can rewrite the files it lints.
server.note_default_is_safe: The audited tool does not write unless the caller asks. Called without `write`, it reports the fix it would make and says so plainly: preview only, call again with write true to save it. This is the fifth per-call switch in the sample that decides whether a tool mutates, after a dedup flag, an overwrite flag, a content digest and a dry-run default, and it is the clearest of them: the tool is read-only by default and mutating on request, with one boolean between the two. No annotation on this tool, or anywhere in the protocol, can express that.
server.note_observer: The effect is a source file rewritten in place, so the plain filesystem observer is canonical and nothing needs projecting.

fixtures.note: The mutating path, reached only by passing `write: true`. The fix is idempotent by construction: it rewrites a declaration to its explicit form, and the rewritten file no longer matches the rule, so a repeat finds nothing to change. Expected indistinguishable, which keeps it out of the duplicate denominator and in the pooled one. `probe_stable` is set because the linter's output is a rule report over the file's contents with no timestamp or generated id; it was checked against the real output. Note the probe reports remaining violations rather than the file, so it shows that something changed and cannot show how many times.
